section.sectionSummaryBrief: This explains why the Tzemach Tzedek did not cite the interpretation that "Yaakov shall take root" refers specifically to mitzvos in exile, because the revelations of the future depend on our service in all times.
section.t: And it may be said,

that this, that in the above discourse of the Tzemach Tzedek he does not copy this interpretation in “Yaakov shall take root” that it refers to the fulfillment of the commandments during the time of exile,
is,
because that the revelations of the future to come depend on our actions and service is in our actions and service in all times,
both in the time of the Holy Temple and in the time of exile,
for in each one of them there is an advantage
(as will be explained below),
and “Yaakov shall take root”
(according to the explanation in this discourse)
refers to the fulfillment of the commandments in all times.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: There are two aspects in the superiority of mitzvos over Torah study: the higher drawing down through mitzvos, and the transformation of darkness to light, with the former being greater in the Temple era and the latter primarily in exile.
section.t: And the concept is,
that in the advantage of the fulfillment of the commandments over the study of Torah,
there are two matters.
That the drawing down through the fulfillment of the commandments is loftier than the drawing down through the study of Torah
(as above in section 1),
and that in the fulfillment of the commandments there is the advantage of the transformation of darkness to light,
for the refinement of the body, the animal soul, and its portion in the world is
(primarily)
through the performance of the commandments24.
And from the distinctions between these two matters,
the drawing down through the fulfillment of the commandments is greater in the time of the Holy Temple than in the time of exile.
For the drawing down through the performance of the commandments is
(primarily)
when the action is in a state of self-nullification25,
and since the matter of self-nullification is primarily in the time of the Holy Temple
[for in addition to that in the time of exile it is impossible to have the self-nullification of prostration
(inner self-nullification)
which comes specifically from the side of the vision of G-dliness,
and as we say26
“and we are unable to ascend and appear and prostrate ourselves before You,”
for since we are unable to ascend and appear, consequently we are unable to prostrate ourselves,
to be in a state of inner self-nullification27,
so too the external self-nullification
(the self-nullification of bowing28),
which comes from the side of the comprehension of G-dliness
(which exists,
in general,
also in the time of exile),
is not as it should be,
since even the comprehension of G-dliness in the time of exile is not true comprehension29],
therefore,
the drawing down through the fulfillment of the commandments in the time of the Holy Temple was a loftier drawing down.
And the primary drawing down through the commandments will be in the future to come,
for then the fulfillment of the commandments will be in ultimate perfection,
as “the commandment of Your will”30.
And the matter of the transformation of darkness to light through the fulfillment of the commandments is primarily in the time of exile.
For the darkness of the body, the animal soul, and the world as they are in exile is a greater darkness than their darkness as they are in their own essence,
and through the fulfillment of the commandments in the time of exile,
by which the refinement of the body etc. as they are in exile is accomplished,
even this darkness is transformed into light.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: In the future, both aspects of mitzvos will be revealed, with the revelation of the light from darkness depending primarily on our service in exile, and the revelation of the Ein Sof in the mitzvos themselves depending primarily on our service in the Temple era.
section.t: And behold, in the future to come there will be the revelation of the two above-mentioned matters in the fulfillment of the commandments,
the revelation of the drawing down through the fulfillment of the commandments itself,
and the revelation of the drawing down through the refinement and transformation that is accomplished through the commandment.
And it may be said that this which is written in Tanya, that the revelations of the future depend on our actions and service in the time of exile,
is,
because in Tanya there it speaks of the superiority of the transformation of darkness to light,
the advantage31
of the light that comes from the darkness32.
And the revelation of this light that will be in the future
(the advantage of the light that comes from the darkness)
depends
(primarily)
on our actions and service in the time of exile,
and that in the future there will be the revelation of the Ein Sof that is in the commandments themselves depends
(primarily)
on our actions and service in the time of the Holy Temple.
